reponse:
I'll look into that.

**What broke:** ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB; with the 512 Mi memory limit the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped. The change went to all pods at once [1]. Events kept arriving in Kafka but were processed late — customer dashboards showed stale data from 08:47 to 12:27 UTC (3h40) [1]. Detection was slow: there was no consumer-lag alert, and the first signal was a Sentry OOM alert at 09:14, 27 minutes after the deploy; a rollback to v2.13.3 at 10:05 drained the lag by 12:27 [1][9].

**Customer data:** no loss. Reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed event counts per workspace matched Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [1][6]. All workspaces saw delayed dashboards; 4 customers contacted support (Orbitly, Zest Grocers, 2 trial accounts) and incident reports went out Nov 15 [1].

**What's changing:**
- ingest#419 (merged Nov 13): default reverted to 1 MB, the batcher refuses any batch over 25% of container memory and logs a warning, bulk import keeps 10 MB via explicit config [7].
- KES-431: page on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Noa, due Nov 20) [1]. The rule is in and routed to on-call, but still being tuned — 5 min fires during every nightly backfill, so it stays In Progress until quiet for 3 nights [10].
- KES-432: ingest config changes go to the canary pool first (Daniel, due Nov 27) [1].
- KES-433: raise worker memory limit to 1 Gi plus a load test on batch sizes (Lior, due Nov 27) [1].
